slides.page_title: Pub/Sub vs Streams: Two Models, One Server

items: Pub/Sub (2.0) and Streams (5.0) share no commands, no keyspace
Channel names are not keys — invisible to `KEYS` and `SCAN`
Channels never reach RDB or AOF; there is nothing to persist
A stream IS a key: has a TTL, dumps to RDB, replays from AOF
Streams replicate as ordinary key data, like a hash or a list

lines: SCAN 0 MATCH jobs          # stream key shows
PUBSUB CHANNELS jobs       # channel lives here

items: Server pushes to whoever is connected now, then forgets
Entry stays in the log until you trim it
Entry stays in the PEL until you `XACK` it
A subscriber joining at t+1 can never see t's message
Append-only log: `XRANGE` any past window on demand
Many independent readers replay the same entries
Pub/Sub memory is freed the instant the push completes

lines: XREAD STREAMS jobs 0     # reader A replays
XREAD STREAMS jobs 0     # reader B, same data
blocks.note: readers never consume each other's entries

items: Borrows Kafka's log model, but one key, in memory
No partitions, no per-topic disk segments
Neither is a broker: no exchanges, no routing keys
No built-in dead-letter queue — you build that yourself
Slow subscriber: output buffer fills, Redis ==disconnects== it
Slow stream reader: just lags on its **own** cursor
The stream keeps the entries; the reader catches up later

blocks.title: Sortable IDs
items: Both keep per-publisher order
Streams add a global `<ms>-<seq>` ID
IDs double as time-range cursors

blocks.title: Rule Of Thumb
blocks.text: Pub/Sub for ephemeral live signals — cache invalidation, presence, tickers. Streams for work that must not be lost — jobs, events, orders.

lines: SUBSCRIBE news.tech      # conn enters sub mode
PSUBSCRIBE news.*        # glob, all news topics

items: `PUBLISH` returns receivers, not deliveries confirmed
That count excludes shard-channel receivers entirely
RESP2 subscriber mode allows only SUBSCRIBE, PING, QUIT, RESET
RESP3 lifts it — push is a distinct protocol type, so normal commands work
Patterns use glob syntax: `*`, `?`, `[abc]`
Subscribed directly AND by pattern? You get it twice
`PUBLISH` is O(N+M): N subscribers plus M registered patterns
Heavy pattern use slows down every single publish

lines: PUBLISH cache:invalidate user:42  # nodes drop it

items: Expiry fires on actual deletion, not at the TTL instant
Lazy access or the active cycle deletes — delay can be seconds
RESP3 client-side caching rides `__redis__:invalidate`
Same mechanism means the same at-most-once caveat

blocks.title: Buffer Limits Kill
items: `client-output-buffer-limit pubsub 32mb 8mb 60`
Over the limit, Redis kills the connection
Everything queued is silently lost
Reconnect must re-issue SUBSCRIBE — the gap is gone

blocks.title: MULTI Does Not Help
blocks.text: Subscribers see the messages after `EXEC`, but no subscriber ever confirms receipt. Transactions bound the publisher, never the delivery.

items: There is no queue sitting behind a channel
Nothing tells you how many messages fell in the deploy gap
Soft limit 8mb for 60s kills the client mid-stream
TCP takes seconds to notice; the publisher sees no error
Replicas propagate Pub/Sub, but promotion drops in-flight messages
Delivered off the socket = done, as far as Redis is concerned
AOF and RDB never record a published message
A restart replays keys and replays no messages at all
`PUBLISH`'s return counts buffered clients, not processed work

slides.page_title: Pub/Sub in Cluster: Sharding & Reconnect Gaps

items: Plain `PUBLISH` reaches ==every node== over the bus
Subscribers may connect to any node and still receive
Cost grows with node count, not subscriber count

blocks.note: client must route to the slot's node

items: A dropped subscriber must re-issue `SUBSCRIBE` itself
Auto-resubscribing libraries still **lose** the gap
No cursor exists to resume from — there is no history

blocks.title: Failover Too
blocks.text: A slot migration or primary promotion drops shard subscribers — they reconnect to the new owner and miss whatever was in flight.

items: Plain `PUBLISH` is correct but costs O(nodes) traffic
A known scaling bottleneck on wide clusters
`SPUBLISH`/`SSUBSCRIBE` (7.0) confine a channel to one slot's shard
Price of that: your client must be slot-aware
Job dispatch on Pub/Sub double-runs every job
Pub/Sub as sole invalidation transport with no TTL fallback
One missed message means a permanently stale cache entry

blocks.title: Treat It As A Hint
blocks.text: Pair Pub/Sub with a short TTL, a version counter, or a periodic reconcile sweep. The moment you need 'did anyone actually handle this?', you need Streams — no tuning buys guarantees.

lines: XADD orders * id 42 amt 19.99  # * = server ID
XADD orders 1526919030474-* id 43  # pin the ms

items: ID is `<ms>-<seq>`: epoch millis plus a 64-bit counter
The seq disambiguates entries inside one millisecond
IDs are strictly monotonic per stream, never reused
Partial IDs give deterministic time bucketing

blocks.title: The Backwards-ID Error
items: `ERR The ID specified in XADD is equal or`
`smaller than the target stream top item`
Seen when replaying a backup with explicit IDs
Fix the cursor with `XSETID`, not with retries

slides.page_title: Streams: Reading the Log & Its Internals

items: An entry is a flat field-value map, like a small hash
No nesting exists at any depth
Serialize structured payloads to JSON or MessagePack
Put that blob in one field — keeps field names stable
`-` is the smallest ID, `+` is the largest
A `(` prefix makes a range bound exclusive
`$` means only entries arriving after this call
`XREAD` is pure fan-out — every reader keeps its own last ID
That cursor lives client-side; Redis stores nothing
N readers all see all entries, and nothing is acknowledged
Entries share one master entry of field names per node
Identical field names are dramatically cheaper than varying ones
`XDEL key id` flags the entry; memory frees when the node empties
`XINFO STREAM key` shows length, nodes, last-generated-id, entries-added
`ENTRIESADDED` restores the lifetime counter behind group `lag`
`MAXDELETEDID` records the highest ID ever removed
Wrong values make `XINFO GROUPS` lag read NULL or lie

blocks.title: Rebuilding A Stream
blocks.text: `XSETID key id [ENTRIESADDED n] [MAXDELETEDID id]` forcibly rewrites the cursor — the one tool for restoring a stream from a backup without breaking monotonicity.

lines: XADD s 1757-0 k v   # re-add from backup
XADD s 1757-1 k v   # explicit IDs, in order
blocks.note: replay IDs ascending or XADD errors

items: A named cursor plus a delivery ledger, stored in the key
One shared last-delivered-id for the whole group
Per-consumer sets of unacknowledged entries alongside it

lines: XGROUP CREATE orders g $ MKSTREAM  # tail only
XGROUP CREATE orders g2 0          # replay all
XREADGROUP GROUP g w1 COUNT 10 STREAMS orders >

items: `$` starts at the tail, `0` replays every entry in the log
Without `MKSTREAM`: `ERR The XGROUP subcommand requires the key to exist`
`>` means entries never delivered to any consumer in this group
Any other ID (usually `0`) reads that consumer's OWN pending entries
Consumers are created implicitly on first `XREADGROUP`
No registration step exists at all
A typo'd name silently creates a consumer that owns nothing
`XGROUP CREATECONSUMER` / `DELCONSUMER` manage them explicitly
`NOACK` skips PEL insertion — at-most-once with group ergonomics
Use `NOACK` only when losing a message is genuinely acceptable
`DELCONSUMER` returns how many pending entries died with it

lines: XREADGROUP GROUP g pod-7 BLOCK 2000 STREAMS s 0
# drain own backlog first, then switch to >
XACK s g 1757-0     # only after work succeeded

slides.page_title: Cursor Surgery, the PEL & Idempotent XACK

items: `SETID` does NOT clear the PEL — old pending entries remain
`DESTROY` leaves stream entries, so another group still reads them
`XINFO GROUPS` reports consumers, pending, entries-read, lag
`lag` = added but not yet delivered; NULL once trimming outran it

blocks.title: Name Consumers Stably
blocks.text: Derive the consumer name from a stable identity — pod name, worker index. A random UUID per process start orphans that consumer's PEL entries on every restart.

items: Per-group table of delivered-but-unacked entries
An entry enters the PEL the instant `XREADGROUP` returns it
That is before your code has seen the bytes on the wire

lines: # 0 means already acked, or never pending

items: Acking an unknown ID is not an error — retry-safe cleanup
At-least-once: crash after work, before ack, means redelivery
Handlers must therefore be idempotent, no exceptions
No exactly-once exists: keep a processed-ID set or a unique constraint

caption.text: `PUBLISH` returning 2 does not mean two workers did the job — it means two sockets got the bytes, and Redis stopped caring. This ten-page field handbook walks the whole Redis messaging surface: why Pub/Sub loses messages six different ways, how consumer groups split work with XREADGROUP and the Pending Entries List, and how to rescue stuck entries with XAUTOCLAIM before your trim policy deletes work nobody ran. Save it before your next queue outage, not after.
